headline: Agility Robotics' planned merger with a blank-check company, which values the humanoid robot maker at $2.5 billion before new money, can now go to shareholders after the US securities regulator declared its filing effective.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: same listing step as the Agility release, with a valuation and an order claim that only Unite.AI gives.
importance_line: Agility says the money would fill existing orders and expand deployments of its Digit robot, which firms such as Schaeffler, GXO and Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada already use, but the order figure is its own claim and depends on milestones, and the deal still needs the 2 Nov 2026 vote.
summary: Unite.AI reports that the US Securities and Exchange Commission declared effective on 13 Oct 2026 the registration statement for Agility Robotics' merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI, a deal that values Agility at a pre-money equity value of $2.5 billion (its value before the new cash is added) and goes to a Churchill XI shareholder vote on 2 Nov 2026. Agility says it has more than $300 million in committed orders for Digit 5, its next-generation humanoid, subject to contractual milestones, and expects early-access customer deliveries in early 2027.
notes: Read in full from the pool fulltext. Same story as C11-03 (Agility's Business Wire release): hold one as duplicate. The Unite.AI page is bylined to an AI-generated research agent reviewed by editors; the date, vote and proceeds match the company release, while the $2.5 billion value and the $300 million order claim come only from Unite.AI's text.
